title: Re-roll: choose the new visual world
question: Magma Chamber, Cyclorama City and Cracktro are out. The roll assigned The Whiteboard Session. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: The Whiteboard Session
options.lineage: the engineer at the whiteboard, explaining how the system works
options.thesis: The whole site is a whiteboard session with Umer. Systems draw themselves in marker as you scroll: boxes, arrows, numbers. Day is a matte white board; night is a dark glass wall with chalk-white ink. Your cursor is a marker; you can draw. It refuses the dark-hero-with-a-floating-3D-object portfolio and the previous cave.
materials: marker ink that draws in stroke by stroke
options.viewport: A clean board. Top-left, the name written in marker. Centre, a live system diagram draws itself: LLM agent → human approval → voice pipeline → multi-tenant SaaS → Kubernetes, with the headline 'I build AI products end to end' in a modern display grotesk. Bottom-left, two sticky notes: 'Hire me' (email + CV) and 'Build with me' (start a project). Right edge, the toolbar: theme, sound, marker colour. Move the mouse and a marker trail follows; click-drag draws on the board and fades.
options.risk: Hand-drawn can read casual if the strokes are sloppy; the strokes, timing and type must be precise and silky. Big diagrams need care on phones.

raised.raise: Every project is explained as numbered assembly steps: prior parts ghosted, the new part bright, an arrow to its seat.
One fixed rhythmic grid and a few decisive type sizes; every control has a physical press.
Two-ink discipline: graphite plus one cobalt marker, rose only for the live highlight.
Two-stage reveal on project cards: pull halfway to peek, open to go deeper.
The grid module is sacred; small screens scale the module, never reflow the diagram.
Nothing disappears: visited sections stay ticked on the board for the visit.

options.label: The Launch Keynote
options.thesis: Each system Umer built is revealed like a flagship product: full-bleed, scroll-driven, real-time demos, one product per act, with a keynote's pacing.
options.viewport: A single line and the name, then the first product rises into frame as you scroll, its numbers counting.
options.risk: This is the direction most portfolios of this ambition land on; familiar and effective.

options.label: Build Instructions
options.thesis: Every product as an exploded assembly: numbered steps, 1:1 call-outs, ghosted prior parts, the new piece bright with an arrow.
options.viewport: Step 1 of AlphaVenue: the API brick drops onto the data-model plate along a dashed arrow.
options.case: Holds product clarity (a client sees exactly how a system assembles); loses audience identification for a recruiter reading a professional profile.
options.risk: Toy grammar can undercut seniority if the type and colour are not disciplined.

options.label: Neubrutalist, award-grade
options.thesis: Bright solids in heavy black outlines on off-white, hard offset shadows, buttons that snap into their shadow, all on one strict grid.
options.viewport: Name in a chunky grotesk inside a black-outlined block; four coloured project blocks below.
options.case: Holds product clarity and reads modern to founders; loses on your steer toward classy and silky, since this world is loud by design.
options.risk: Very recognisable style; reads as a trend.

options.label: Jet-age Ticket Wallet
options.lineage: airline ticket wallets with carbon-copy coupons
options.case: Charming, but neither recruiters nor product clients identify with paper coupons, and numbers in carbon fields lose clarity.

options.label: Risograph
options.case: A print world for a software engineer; the misregistration device reads as decoration against a tech-savvy brief.

options.label: Teletext Magazine
options.case: Retro novelty; a bitmap face cannot carry the CV's prose or a classy register.

options.label: Sneaker Box Wall
options.lineage: stacked sneaker boxes with end labels
options.case: Collector grammar; the audience does not shop for an engineer this way.
options.kept: Peek, then open: a two-stage reveal.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Dark hero, big name, a floating 3D object, a project grid, a contact form; executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Centered name over a rotating 3D object, three project cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from ten thousand developer portfolios by design.
